html:
Equatorial Guinea became independent from Spain on 12 October 1968, joining the island of Bioko and the mainland province of Río Muni into one republic.

Spain under Franco had made the colony two provinces of Spain in 1959 and granted it self-rule in 1963, under pressure from the United Nations. A constitution was approved in a referendum, and in the only free election for decades Francisco Macías Nguema won the presidency.

Within months, rows with Spain led most Spaniards to leave, taking money and skills with them. The joining of the islanders and the far larger Fang mainland stayed uneasy. Macías soon ruled by terror, and the country fell out of sight until the oil boom.
sum: Equatorial Guinea became independent from Spain on 12 October 1968, joining the island of Bioko and the mainland province of Río Muni into one republic.
